title: Reorder Log Files
prompt: You are given an array of log strings. Each log has an identifier followed by words or numbers. Reorder the logs so that all letter-logs come before digit-logs, letter-logs are sorted lexicographically by content then identifier, and digit-logs keep their original order.

examples.input: logs = ["dig1 8 1 5 1","let1 art can","dig2 3 6","let2 own kit dig","let3 art zero"]
examples.output: ["let1 art can","let3 art zero","let2 own kit dig","dig1 8 1 5 1","dig2 3 6"]

complexity_target: Parse each log once and use sorting only where needed for letter-logs.

title: Top K Frequent Items
prompt: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent values. The order of the result does not matter.
constraints: k is in the range [1, number of unique values]
complexity_target: Avoid repeatedly sorting the full array of frequencies if possible.

title: Search Suggestions System
prompt: Given a list of product names and a search word, return up to three product suggestions after each character of the search word is typed. Suggestions must share the typed prefix and be returned in lexicographic order.
constraints: All strings contain lowercase English letters
complexity_target: Avoid scanning the full product list from scratch for every prefix if possible.

title: Word Ladder
prompt: Given two words beginWord and endWord and a dictionary wordList, return the length of the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord. Only one letter may change at a time, and each transformed word must exist in the dictionary.

starter_template.name: ladderLength
starter_template.typescript_params: beginWord: string, endWord: string, wordList: string[]
starter_template.python_params: beginWord: str, endWord: str, wordList: list[str]
starter_template.java_signature: int ladderLength(String beginWord, String endWord, List<String> wordList)
starter_template.csharp_signature: int LadderLength(string beginWord, string endWord, IList<string> wordList)

complexity_target: Use BFS and avoid comparing every word against every other word directly.
